findings.title: `BrowserReportSerializer` neither requires `age` nor `timestamp`, and mishandles `0` values
findings.body:
`BrowserReportSerializer` defines both `age` and `timestamp` with `required=False` and validates mutual exclusivity in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` using truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`). This has two bugs:
1. If a report omits both `age` and `timestamp`, neither field validator runs and the serializer accepts the report even though both W3C Reporting specs require one of them.
2. If a report has `age: 0` (very common for newly generated reports) along with `timestamp`, `self.initial_data.get("age")` is `0` (falsy), so `validate_timestamp` will not reject the mixed report (and likewise for `timestamp: 0`, which is explicitly allowed by `min_value=0`).

Check `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or `is not None`) and add an object-level `validate` method ensuring exactly one of `age` or `timestamp` is provided.

findings.title: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` mispairs or drops events when nodestore misses or reorders keys
findings.body: In `fetch_error_details`, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` (and some backends only include found keys or do not guarantee key order matching `node_ids`). Iterating with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs `error_ids` positionally with `events.values()` instead of looking up each `node_id` in `events`. If any event is missing from nodestore or returned in a different order, `event_id` will be associated with the wrong event's payload or events will be silently dropped. Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

findings.title: `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` references undefined `PRCommentWorkflow`
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, and calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, while `_truncate_title` was defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (not `PRCommentWorkflow`, which isn't even imported or defined in `commit_context.py`). Calling `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` from `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` or `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` will either raise `NameError: name 'PRCommentWorkflow' is not defined` (if `PRCommentWorkflow` is not in module scope) or `AttributeError` if `PRCommentWorkflow` does not inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`. Call `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` (or make it a `@classmethod` and call `cls._truncate_title(title)`).

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, when `searchQuery.trim()` is empty (lines 61-63), `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly without filtering out `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`['is_segment', 'project_id', 'received']`). The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check is only applied in the non-empty search branch (lines 65-69), so `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` remain visible by default and only disappear once the user types into the search box. Filter out `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` before checking `searchQuery.trim()`.
